findings.F1: Over 3 days, a 24h fall on wide bars is followed by an excess return that grows with how wide the bars are against their 30-day mean. On the 18-bar grid, falls whose 24h bar range is 1.5 to 2 times its 30-day mean returned +2.1 % above the coin's drift (t 2.48, n 156). At 2 to 3 times it was +3.4 % (t 3.45, n 58). Below 1 times it was −0.5 % to −0.1 % (t −1.24 and −0.35). The plan's own 3x-and-above level gave only +1.1 % (t 1.09, n 34). Rises on the same widths showed nothing (all |t| < 1.7).
findings.F2: The fall's depth matters only once the bars are wide. With bars over 1.5 times their usual width, a 24h fall of 1 to 2 usual 24h moves returned +4.7 % over 3 days (t 3.51, n 60), and a fall beyond 2 usual moves returned +2.4 % (t 3.40, n 134). The same falls on bars of normal width returned +0.4 % (t 0.80, n 239) and +0.3 % (t 0.30, n 16). Shallow falls under 1 usual move returned −0.7 % (t −0.50).
findings.F3: The rebound after a panic comes almost entirely from coins that were rising beforehand.
findings.F4: The wide-bar fall effect sits in the smaller coins and is uneven across years.
findings.F5: The 4h bar from 20:00 to 24:00 UTC returns more than the coin's mean 4h return, consistently across coins and years.
findings.F6: The 4h bar from 00:00 to 04:00 UTC returns less than the coin's mean.
findings.F7: The tested book's problem is too few trades, not the size of the move.

ideas.idea: A 24-hour fall in which the coin's bars are wider than their 30-day average is followed by higher than usual returns over the next 3 days. The wider the bars against their 30-day average, the higher the return, already from moderately widened ranges, well below several times the usual size.
ideas.consequence: A trader should buy 24-hour falls on unusually wide bars even when the range has not reached panic size, more so the wider the bars, and refuse falls on bars of normal width.
ideas.name: wide-range falls rebound

ideas.idea: Among 24-hour falls on unusually wide bars, the higher the coin's 30-day return before the fall, the higher its return over the next 3 days. Falls that interrupt a 30-day rise give the largest rebound.
ideas.consequence: A trader should take wide-range dips in a coin that was rising over the past 30 days, more so the stronger the rise, and refuse them in a coin already falling.
ideas.name: wide-range dip in uptrend

ideas.idea: Over the 4 hours from 20:00 to 24:00 UTC, the coin returns more than its usual 4-hour return. The larger the coin's 24-hour move up to 20:00 UTC, in either direction, the larger that excess.
ideas.consequence: A trader who is already deciding to buy should time the purchase before 20:00 UTC, more so after a large 24-hour move, and avoid selling into that hour.
ideas.name: late-UTC evening bid

ideas.idea: Over the 4 hours from 00:00 to 04:00 UTC, the coin returns less than its usual 4-hour return. The larger the coin's absolute 24-hour return up to midnight UTC, the larger that shortfall.
ideas.consequence: A trader who is already deciding to buy should prefer to wait until after 04:00 UTC rather than buy at midnight UTC, more so after a large 24-hour move.
ideas.name: post-midnight UTC weakness
